document.name: Fun Mini Soccer - Master Product and Engineering Specification
document.purpose: Dokumen instruksi untuk Codex membangun web app pengelolaan kompetisi mini soccer yang fleksibel, mobile-first, dan dapat dipakai publik.
document.instruction_for_codex: Implementasikan aplikasi berdasarkan spesifikasi ini ketika pengguna memerintahkan pembangunan. Jangan berhenti pada mockup atau halaman statis. Buat aplikasi fungsional dengan database, autentikasi, izin akses, generator fixture, kontrol skor, kalkulasi klasemen, bracket, realtime, serta automated tests. Jika repo sudah ada, audit dan pertahankan struktur yang relevan. Jangan mengklaim fitur berfungsi tanpa menjalankan pengujian. Dokumentasikan keputusan dan asumsi yang belum diputuskan; gunakan default yang eksplisit dalam dokumen ini. Jangan menggunakan tim, hasil, jadwal, atau URL contoh sebagai data produksi.

product.name: Fun Mini Soccer
product.category: Open multi-tenant football competition management platform
product.primary_objective: Memudahkan penyelenggara membuat kompetisi dan memperbarui hasil setiap pertandingan sehingga peserta dan penonton mudah memantau skor, jadwal, klasemen, dan bracket.
principles: Simple for organizers, informative for players and spectators
Quick Competition first; advanced settings optional
One user can manage many independently configured competitions
Spectators can view public competitions without accounts
Match data and permissions are enforced on the server
Presets are defaults, not restrictive rules
out_of_scope_mvp: Permanent team identity and ownership claims
Player registration, lineups, and player performance history

technology.authentication: Supabase Auth: email-password and Google OAuth if configured
technology.realtime: Supabase Realtime for competition and match subscriptions
technology.hosting: Vercel for Next.js, Supabase for data/auth/realtime
technology.validation: Zod schemas shared across forms and server boundaries
technology.testing: Vitest for unit/integration, Playwright for E2E
technology.schema_migrations: Versioned SQL migrations committed to repository
technology.package_management: Use package manager already present; otherwise pnpm
technology.security_note: Never expose service role key to browser, logs, client bundles, or public API responses. OAuth depends on provider configuration; provide setup documentation.

users_and_permissions.registration: Open signup, login, logout, password reset and email verification where configured

roles.visitor: May browse publicly listed competitions and view unlisted competitions through link without login, subject to visibility rules
roles.registered_user: May create and own competitions, edit own profile, and manage competition roles as granted
roles.competition_owner: Full control of owned competition, its settings, members, scheduling, scoring, publication and archive
roles.competition_admin: Manage competition teams, schedules, rules and results, but cannot transfer ownership or delete competition
roles.score_operator: Start and end games, update live scores, and submit corrections with audit trail; cannot change rules or invite admins
roles.platform_moderator: Handle reports and abusive content through protected platform-only access

users_and_permissions.role_scope: Roles are per competition, not global, except platform_moderator
users_and_permissions.membership_invitation: Owner/admin can invite existing users by email or generate expiring secure invite links; permission assignment must be verified server-side
access_control: All writes authenticate the user and check competition-scoped permission with RLS and server actions
No user can change another user's competition without authorized membership
Guests never see edit controls or access private content
Revoked invite or member loses permission immediately
Prevent last owner from removing self without ownership transfer
Do not trust client-provided owner_id, role, result state, or computed standings

visibility.public: Visible in discovery and through direct URL
visibility.unlisted: Accessible by direct link without login, not indexed in internal discovery
visibility.private: Accessible only to explicitly authorized signed-in members; links alone do not grant access

competition.publication: Starts in draft. Organizer reviews teams, rules and generated fixtures before explicit publication.

team_model_mvp.validation: Names required and unique case-insensitively within one competition; unrelated competitions may repeat team names
team_model_mvp.future_upgrade: Schema may later reference permanent team profiles; preserve historical display-name and logo snapshots

competition_rule_defaults.ranking_tiebreak_note: Use documented deterministic rules. Multi-team head-to-head needs a mini-table with clear scope; manual resolution must be recorded and audited.
competition_rule_defaults.champion_declaration: Optional for round-robin formats; don't force champion declaration for casual events

fourfeo.description: Convenience preset for exactly four teams, using round-robin pairs; amount of meetings is chosen by organizer.
fourfeo.allowed_meetings_per_pair: Any organizer-selected positive integer within configurable operational limits; do not hardcode one or two only
fourfeo.formula: total_matches = n*(n-1)/2 * meetings_per_pair; for fourfeo n=4
fourfeo.classification: One combined table across all meetings when ranking_enabled=true

league.meetings_per_pair: Organizer picks one, two, or more meetings
league.home_away: Where meaningful, reverse displayed sides on alternating meetings; no requirement for actual home venue

group_stage.groups: User chooses number of groups and team allocations before publishing fixtures
group_stage.within_group_format: Round-robin with configurable meetings per pair
group_stage.group_assignment: Manual or automated balanced allocation; offer review prior to publish
group_stage.allow_uneven_groups: Explicitly support uneven distribution or show a clear validation error if chosen rule requires equal sizes

knockout.bracket: Single-elimination bracket with optional third-place game
knockout.team_count: At least 2, including non powers of two
knockout.byes: Generate documented byes for non-power-of-two fields
knockout.winner_requirement: A completed knockout match must have an unambiguous advancing participant; regular time tie alone cannot advance a team
knockout.advancement: Automatic, transactional, consistent with bracket edges
knockout.correction_rule: If correcting a feeder result would alter an already-started downstream match, block and require explicit administrative resolution rather than overwriting history

group_then_knockout.qualification: Organizer sets how many advance per group, with clear bracket mapping
group_then_knockout.transition: Freeze/approve qualified teams before generating or confirming knockout bracket
group_then_knockout.tie_handling: Use group ranking tie-break sequence; require recorded resolution when tied on all rules

fixture_engine.round_robin_algorithm: Circle-method or another complete deterministic pair-generation algorithm, then multiply by meetings_per_pair and alternate display side when configured
fixture_engine.manual_reorder: Allow moving fixtures independently of meeting number and without changing their stable IDs; mobile up/down controls and desktop drag/drop with keyboard alternative
fixture_engine.rest_warning: Warn, do not prohibit, when the same team plays consecutive games. Rest optimization is best effort and should not claim zero consecutive appearances are always possible.
fixture_engine.after_start_rule: Keep finished/in-progress fixtures anchored and allow only safe rescheduling of future fixtures without wiping recorded scores
fixture_engine.fixture_regeneration: Preview changes and require confirmation; preserve completed match IDs/results, refuse destructive changes without explicit handling
constraints: Every scheduled match references valid teams in same competition
Schedule order is distinct from match identity

match_management.live_score: Authorized operator adjusts nonnegative integer home/away score; changes become visible on public page promptly after server persistence
match_management.direct_final: Operator can enter score after match without activating LIVE, then must confirm final result
match_management.final_confirmation: Explicit confirmation modal summarizing fixture, score, and any knockout winner decision; only confirmed final score enters official standings
match_management.live_standings: Not official: live matches must not change official standings; optional future provisional mode is out of MVP
match_management.final_score_correction: Dedicated authenticated correction flow with reason, before/after values, actor, timestamp and audit log; recalculate standings atomically
match_management.concurrent_editing: Optimistic version check or transactional locking prevents silent lost updates from multiple operators; show conflict and fetch latest data
match_management.offline_handling: Show connection, save status and retry affordance; never claim a change is saved until server confirms. Full offline write queue is not required in MVP.
match_management.simultaneous_live_matches: Support multiple live games by data model, even if operator UI favors one selected match at a time
validation: No standings update from unconfirmed scores

standings.source_of_truth: Calculate from official final matches; never maintain manually editable points totals

calculation.played: Number of final matches involving team in corresponding stage/group
calculation.points: wins * win_points + draws * draw_points + losses * loss_points
calculation.sort: points descending, then configured tie-breakers applied deterministically
calculation.cancelled_and_postponed: Exclude from played, points, goals and rankings
calculation.draw: Both sides receive draw_points; knockout matches have advancement outcome separate from regulation score

standings.initial_state: All teams visible with zero games and zero points
standings.ranking_resolution: If all automated tie-breakers are equal, display unresolved tie and require explicit tournament-resolution decision when determining champion or qualifiers; avoid silently selecting based on entry order

ui_ux.appearance: Premium, clean, modern sports utility interface with strong typography and minimal decoration
principles: Clear singular primary CTA per screen
Accessible keyboard interaction and focus visibility
Loading, empty, error and success states on every workflow

responsive.mobile: Single-column cards, bottom primary navigation, compact fixture lists, large score steppers
responsive.desktop: Top navigation or left sidebar, wider tables, optional side-by-side score control and fixtures

pages_and_routes.purpose: Brand, hero CTA, live/current competitions, latest fixtures and discovery entry
Search and filter public competitions by title, format and status
Create user account with validation and terms notice
Own/shared competitions, filter active/completed/draft, new competition CTA
Name, visibility, format, regulations, teams, fixtures, preview and publish
Summary, current/live match, latest results, next match, progress and share
All fixtures by stage, status, score and order
Knockout rounds and advancement; hide when inapplicable
Add/edit participant names and optional logos
Generate, preview, reorder, reschedule safely, publish
Live status, score steppers, direct final, confirmation, audited corrections
Rules, visibility, metadata, archival lifecycle with protection for active matches

database_schema.notes: All IDs UUID, created_at and updated_at timestamps where relevant, foreign keys and unique indexes. Follow RLS isolation by competition and define update privileges by membership.
data_integrity: FK participants belong to match competition
Published competition requires valid generated schedule
Competition settings edits cannot corrupt started brackets
Unique fixture pair per meeting within a round-robin stage and group
Public read policies exclude private competitions

server_operations: Add/edit/remove simple teams before locked stages
Generate round-robin fixtures and knockout bracket server-side
Start match and update live score with row_version compare-and-swap
Finalize match once, record audit log and publish realtime updates
Correct final score with reason, audit, recalculation and downstream bracket safeguards
Invite/revoke members with per-competition role checks
Compute standings with deterministic configured tie-breakers
Advance bracket winner atomically after valid final resolution
Search public competitions while excluding unlisted and private from results

subscriptions: Completed match events triggering standings refresh
rules: Optimistic UI must reconcile with server and rollback on error
Reconnect and refetch snapshot after network interruption

organizer: Choose create competition or Quick Fourfeo
Select basic points and optional advanced rules
Reorder fixtures and review rest warnings
Start matches or submit direct final scores
spectator: Open public competition directly or find on Explore
Refresh not required for realtime updates
Can share URL without logging in
score_operator: Start live or choose direct final
Use audited correction flow if necessary

fixture_generation: Fourfeo 4 teams and 1 meeting produces exactly 6 unique pairings
Fourfeo 4 teams and 2 meetings produces exactly 12 matches and each team appears in 6
Fourfeo 4 teams and 3 meetings produces exactly 18 matches
Changing display_order never changes match ID, pair, or scores
Rest-warning accurately identifies adjacent fixtures sharing a team
League double round-robin pairs each opponent twice
Group fixtures remain within their group
Knockout with non-power-of-two teams assigns byes without phantom played matches
scoring_and_rankings: 0-0 scheduled match has no standings impact
Live score appears publicly but official table remains unchanged
Confirming Garuda FC 2-1 Elang FC gives Garuda FC 3 points, played 1, GD +1; Elang 0 points, GD -1
Final correction to Garuda FC 1-1 Elang FC makes both receive 1 point and updates GD to 0
All standings aggregate both meetings for Fourfeo
Postponed and cancelled matches never count as played
Final knockout tie without recorded advancing winner cannot populate next round
Downstream started bracket match is protected against unsafe feeder correction
Same-score rank ties do not silently select a champion
access_and_security: Unauthenticated visitor can see public competition
Unlisted competition is absent from Explore but reachable by direct URL
Private competition is not visible to unauthorized visitor even with slug
Unauthorized user cannot update score through direct server request
Score operator cannot change competition rules
Admin cannot transfer owner status without owner permission
Private realtime channels and server responses do not leak scores
Concurrent score updates detect conflict, not silent overwrite
quality: Mobile score steppers meet 44px touch targets
All public and admin pages have loading/empty/error states
Keyboard navigation and focus indicators work
Playwright E2E flows pass for owner, operator and visitor
Typecheck, lint and production build pass
No seeded sample competition appears in production
README includes setup, env variables, Supabase migration and deployment instructions

simulation_reference_only.usage: Use this data only in local demo seed/test fixtures; never publish as a real competition by default.

definition_of_done.functional: An independent organizer can register, create public Fourfeo with four teams and two meetings, auto-generate and reorder 12 fixtures, publish, update live and final scores, see correct standings, share public page and archive results. Other formats must also pass format-specific tests.
definition_of_done.reliability: No unauthorized writes, score loss, hidden RLS failures, fabricated success notifications or corrupt bracket advancement.
delivery: No hardcoded example results in production
definition_of_done.reporting: At each phase explain completed work, files changed, tests actually run with results, current limitations, and next steps. Never describe an unimplemented feature as complete.
